name: Marsha Blackburn
bio: Tennessee's senior U.S. senator since 2019, Blackburn is the polling frontrunner with broad establishment support and statewide name recognition. Trump-aligned conservative.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Blackburn supports school choice and parental rights in education but has no specific pre-K or childcare proposal in her gubernatorial campaign. She emphasizes personalized learning and opposes federal control of education, backing the Education Freedom Scholarship expansion.
early_childhood_ed.details: As of June 2026, Blackburn holds a commanding 63% lead in the Republican primary poll with August 6 primary approaching. She supports expanding public charter schools to suburban and rural areas and backs the Education Freedom Scholarship program (Gov. Lee expanded it to 35,000 seats in May 2026). She has not released a pre-K or state childcare funding plan. Her OBBB support includes the enhanced Child Tax Credit and childcare tax provisions, which she frames as family relief. No new early childhood education policy announcements were found in June 2026 beyond existing positions.

child_hunger.summary: Blackburn voted for the OBBB which included SNAP cuts she frames as anti-waste and anti-fraud. Tennessee received federal approval for a SNAP food restriction demonstration project effective July 31, 2026, banning candy, soft drinks, and other high-sugar items — part of Secretary Rollins' 'Make America Healthy Again' waivers. Blackburn has supported this approach.
child_hunger.details: Blackburn stated the OBBB is 'rooting out waste, fraud and abuse' and removing access for 'fraudsters, freeloaders and illegal immigrants.' Tennessee received federal approval for a SNAP food restriction demonstration project effective July 31, 2026, banning candy, soft drinks, and other high-sugar items from SNAP purchases — part of Secretary Rollins' 'Make America Healthy Again' waivers. Roughly 695,000 Tennesseans are enrolled in SNAP. Previously, in October 2025, Blackburn supported the Keep SNAP Funded Act during the government shutdown. The Tennessee legislature's April 2026 $7 million allocation for Summer EBT in 2027 drew no statement from Blackburn.

parental_support.summary: Blackburn's signature parental support positions remain the Working Families Tax Cuts embedded in the One Big Beautiful Bill: a permanent, expanded Child Tax Credit ($2,200), enhanced employer childcare tax credit, and a paid family and medical leave credit. The Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act she co-sponsored was signed into law in 2026, streamlining pediatric Medicaid enrollment across state lines.
parental_support.details: Blackburn's Senate statement on the One Big Beautiful Bill highlighted the enhanced child tax credit made permanent as a key win for Tennessee families. The Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act, which Blackburn co-sponsored, was signed into law by President Trump in 2026 as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act; it creates a streamlined pathway for pediatric providers to enroll in multiple state Medicaid programs, reducing delays for children needing specialized care. She also champions the Kids Online Safety Act as a digital-age parental support measure. No new parental support proposals specific to her governor campaign were found beyond reiterating federal-level accomplishments.

name: John Rose
bio: Four-term congressman from the Cumberland Plateau leaving his House seat to run. Farmer and small-business owner from Cookeville.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Rose has no specific early childhood education or pre-K proposal. His education platform centers on school choice, appointing a Tennessee-certified education commissioner, and CTE. He polls at approximately 10% vs. Blackburn's 63% in June 2026 Republican primary polling.
early_childhood_ed.details: Rose has been the first major candidate to enter the 2026 governor's race and consistently emphasizes parental freedom to choose public, charter, private, or homeschool options. He supports the Education Freedom Scholarship alongside Blackburn. No specific pre-K or childcare investment proposal has been identified in Rose's platform. He received a 100% Family Research Council Action rating. No new early childhood specifics emerged in June 2026.

child_hunger.summary: Rose supports scrutinizing how SNAP benefits are spent and has expressed alignment with Tennessee's new SNAP food restriction policy banning sugary items effective July 31, 2026. He frames restrictions as ensuring benefits serve their intended nutritional purpose.
child_hunger.details: In a WJHL interview, Rose stated SNAP benefits 'are supposed to be used for supplemental nutrition, which does not include sugary treats,' and that it is 'right to take a careful look at how the money is used.' Tennessee's SNAP food restriction demonstration project — banning candy, soda, and other high-sugar items — takes effect July 31, 2026, aligning with his stated position. No new June 2026 statements specifically on child hunger beyond this were found.

parental_support.summary: Rose pledges to make Tennessee a national leader in adoption, improve the Department of Children's Services, and protect children from what he calls gender ideology. His FRC 100% rating and stated commitment to faith, family, and freedom define his parental support framing.
parental_support.details: Rose has pledged to improve DCS and make 'Tennessee a national leader when it comes to making adoption attainable for Tennessee families.' He cites the U.S. v. Skremetti Supreme Court ruling affirming states' power to restrict gender transition treatments for minors as a family protection victory. As with early childhood ed and child hunger, no specific childcare subsidy, paid leave, or parental financial support proposals have been identified in his campaign platform.

name: Monty Fritts
bio: East Tennessee state legislator running on a populist conservative platform. Lower profile statewide than Blackburn or Rose.
photo_credit: No headshot found at direct image URL; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Fritts is the only Republican gubernatorial candidate opposing the Education Freedom Scholarship, calling it 'fiscally irresponsible' and 'unconstitutional.' He has no early childhood education or childcare specific proposals and emphasizes returning schools to academic fundamentals. He polls at approximately 5% in the Republican primary.
early_childhood_ed.details: Fritts opposes the Education Freedom Scholarship citing Article XI, Section 12 of the Tennessee Constitution, and voted against its expansion in the legislature. He pledges to suspend or end the voucher program if elected. His education platform emphasizes student achievement, teacher empowerment, parental responsibility, and returning to reading, writing, math, and civics — but contains no pre-K, childcare, or early childhood investment proposals. No new early childhood education policy developments found in June 2026.

child_hunger.summary: No specific positions on child hunger, SNAP, or Summer EBT have been found for Fritts. His limited-government platform and opposition to new spending programs suggests opposition to SNAP expansion, though no direct statement has been identified.
child_hunger.details: Fritts's limited-government, anti-spending platform ('Liberty & Less Government') and his support for eliminating programs he deems unconstitutional or fiscally irresponsible suggest he would not support expanded SNAP benefits or Summer EBT participation. However, no direct public statements or votes on child hunger, SNAP, or food insecurity have been found. He supports eliminating the grocery tax, which would provide some indirect food affordability relief. No new information found in June 2026.

parental_support.summary: Fritts gained national attention in January 2026 for calling for capital punishment for parents of transgender children and providers of gender-affirming care, framing the position as scripturally mandated. In June 2026, he was linked to Tennessee's designation of June as 'Nuclear Family Month' as part of continued anti-LGBTQ+ legislative positioning.
parental_support.details: In January 2026, Fritts called for state-sanctioned executions of parents, guardians, and medical professionals connected to gender-affirming care for minors under age 18, stating the position 'aligns with scripture.' The remarks drew widespread national condemnation. In June 2026, Tennessee lawmakers designated June as 'Nuclear Family Month' rather than Pride Month, with Fritts again cited in that context. His campaign platform states 'parents are the first and final voice in their children's education' and supports parental choice in education without taxpayer-funded vouchers.

name: Lauren Pinkston
bio: Independent gubernatorial candidate. Former Lipscomb University professor with a detailed family-economic platform — only candidate proposing redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to early childhood ed and employer on-site daycare.
photo_credit: Direct headshot URL not found; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pinkston strongly supports redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to expand early childhood education programs and supports businesses offering on-site daycare through state investment. She is endorsed by the Forward Party.
early_childhood_ed.details: Pinkston explicitly stated she is against the Education Freedom Scholarship and would 'invest those funds in early childhood programs desperately needed across the state.' She also supports backing businesses that offer on-site daycare, arguing it expands the workforce through dual-income households and eases financial pressure on families with young children. Her platform on pinkstonfortn.com confirms these positions as of mid-2026. No new June 2026 announcements beyond established platform positions found.

child_hunger.summary: Pinkston opposes Tennessee's new SNAP food restriction waiver (effective July 31, 2026), warning purchase restrictions would harm local grocers and drive up food costs. She supports reinstating Summer EBT linked to Tennessee farmers and would incentivize nutrition education with additional SNAP benefits.
child_hunger.details: Pinkston's platform explicitly opposes restricting SNAP benefits from purchasing snacks or sodas, warning such rules 'harm local grocers and drive up food costs for middle-class families.' Tennessee's SNAP food restriction demonstration project — banning candy, soda, and other items — takes effect July 31, 2026; Pinkston's established position stands against this approach. She supports Summer EBT reinstatement tied to Tennessee farmers, and would offer additional SNAP funds to families who participate in nutrition classes. She also supports exploring grocery tax removal.

parental_support.summary: Pinkston supports eliminating benefit cliffs at DHS to prevent families from losing assistance when income rises modestly, redirecting EFS funds to early childhood education and employer daycare, and protecting TennCare coverage for the 50% of Tennessee children insured through the program. She also supports IVF and contraceptive access and collective bargaining rights.
parental_support.details: Pinkston has warned that TennCare premium increases under federal cuts would be 'a tragedy' for Tennessee's 50%-plus of children covered by the program and pledged to protect it. She supports IVF and contraceptive access as family planning rights, noting she is the aunt of two IVF children. Her benefit cliff reform plan calls on DHS to restructure public assistance so parents are not forced to choose between a raise and losing their benefits. She supports collective bargaining rights, framing worker rights as family stability. No new June 2026 developments found.

name: Jerri Green
bio: Democratic primary frontrunner running a coalition campaign rooted in West Tennessee. Focused on healthcare, education, and rural-urban balance.
photo_credit: Green for Governor official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Green maintains the strongest early childhood education platform in the 2026 field. She calls for universal pre-K statewide, a dedicated childcare and early education fund for households under $75,000, and a Day One commitment to invest $50M in TANF funds to clear the childcare waitlist. She is the Democratic primary frontrunner.
early_childhood_ed.details: Green's 'Day One Plan' centers on deploying $50 million in TANF funds to eliminate the childcare waitlist (which was implemented August 26, 2025 for the Smart Steps program). She proposes a dedicated childcare and early education fund including afterschool and summer care for households under $75K annually, statewide Pre-K expansion, paid family leave, and a living wage. A February 16, 2026 WJHL interview confirmed she wants subsidies for families below the poverty line and living wages for childcare workers. She successfully won Pre-K class funding in Memphis on the City Council. No new June 2026 announcements beyond established platform found.

child_hunger.summary: Green has pledged to budget state funds to cover SNAP and EBT gaps for Tennesseans cut by the One Big Beautiful Bill, directly citing that 1 in 5 Tennessee children go to bed hungry. She opposes the SNAP food restriction waiver and supports ending the grocery tax. She urged Gov. Lee to suspend the grocery tax during the federal shutdown.
child_hunger.details: In her February 16, 2026 WJHL policy interview, Green stated she would 'budget to fund those in need of SNAP/EBT benefits who were affected by the Big Beautiful Bill.' She stated: '1 in 5 kids right now in the state of Tennessee goes to bed hungry.' She sent a November 2025 letter to Gov. Lee urging suspension of the 4% grocery tax during a federal shutdown. Her Day One Plan includes $50M in TANF funds for the childcare waitlist, which also addresses food security indirectly. She opposes the Tennessee SNAP food restriction waiver (effective July 31, 2026) as harmful to families.

parental_support.summary: Green's 'One Tough Mother' brand anchors a platform of paid family leave, childcare access, free diapers and ending the diaper tax, gun lock distribution, expanded Medicaid, and $10M in TANF-funded housing relief to stabilize families. She is the Democratic primary frontrunner at 14% with 62% of Democrats still undecided.
parental_support.details: Green's Day One Plan deploys $10 million in TANF funds to waive security deposits for 100,000+ Tennessee families, $50 million to eliminate the childcare waitlist, $10 million to erase predatory medical debt, and an executive order to protect women's healthcare access. She supports paid family leave, affordable childcare, living wages, and expanded Medicaid. She was appointed Interim Chief Public Defender for Shelby County by Mayor Lee Harris in January 2026. She also proposes a Special Education Equity Fund and distributes free gun locks. No new June 2026 parental support announcements found.

name: Dr. Carnita Atwater
bio: Memphis community advocate making her second gubernatorial run. Known for community development work in the New Chicago neighborhood.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific early childhood education or childcare policy positions have been found for Atwater. Her platform references vocational training. Her 30+ years of community advocacy for children informs her broad stance, but she has not translated this into gubernatorial policy proposals.
early_childhood_ed.details: No specific pre-K, childcare, or early childhood education proposals have been recorded for Atwater on Ballotpedia, or her campaign website. Her campaign frames her candidacy around community advocacy experience, including decades serving children, seniors, homeless youth, and LGBTQ+ youth. She has fostered 92 children and currently serves as community mother to 125+ children in North Memphis. No new June 2026 education policy statements found.

child_hunger.summary: Atwater's Ballotpedia survey response proposes 'portable food satellites in every food desert.' A justmymemphis.com profile notes she pledges to 'release withheld funds for food assistance' and prioritize low-income families in state budgets. No SNAP-specific positions or Summer EBT statements were found.
child_hunger.details: Atwater's most specific food policy proposal remains the 'portable food satellites in every food desert' from her Ballotpedia survey — a community-service model consistent with her founding of food programs for elderly Memphis residents. She pledges to 'release withheld funds for food assistance' and frames budgets as 'moral documents' with spending priorities shifted toward vulnerable populations, but without SNAP-specific details. No statements on the OBBB SNAP cuts, the Summer EBT gap, or the SNAP food restriction waiver (effective July 31, 2026) were found.

parental_support.summary: Atwater has no specific parental support policy proposals — no paid leave, childcare subsidy, or family financial support programs are articulated. Her campaign draws on her personal history of fostering 92 children and her calling for better halfway services to bridge gaps for youth aging out of foster care.
parental_support.details: Atwater's most distinctive family credential is her personal history of fostering 92 children, which she says gives her deep understanding of low-income family challenges. Her campaign materials describe decades of direct service — feeding, clothing, sheltering, and advocating for families. She calls for addressing foster care system gaps, particularly establishing better halfway services for children aging out of the system. She has sheltered over 100 domestic violence victims. No specific gubernatorial policy proposals on parental leave, childcare, or family financial support were found.
